cases.title: Drop blamed on temporary destocking, but a major customer is also insourcing
reasons: The price drop appears to be partially structural, not purely temporary as the thesis requires: a second-largest customer (15% of sales) has announced a permanent move to its own in-house platform from 2027, which represents structural loss of revenue, not temporary customer destocking.

Management attributes the profit warning to temporary destocking, but the concurrent customer platform migration announcement (announced in the same quarter) suggests a more fundamental challenge that contradicts the thesis criterion that the reason for the price fall 'must be temporary.'
All kill criteria are clear and not met: leverage is 2.0x (well below 4x), no holder above 25%, and no regulatory issue.
The company fits the segment (in-vitro diagnostics instruments and immunoassay assays) and meets the recurring revenue requirement (75% of sales, above the 50% threshold).
missing_facts: What proportion of the 35% stock decline is driven by the customer loss announcement versus the destocking profit warning, and whether the market differentiated between temporary and structural factors.
Whether this customer platform migration is an isolated incident or part of a broader trend of customers developing in-house alternatives, which would confirm structural decline.
The company's retention and replacement strategy for the 15% revenue at risk, and whether they have pipeline opportunities to offset this loss.
